hints: Focus on splitting the ester at the single C-O bond, the acid part keeps the C=O and the alcohol part keeps the O.
Count carbons on the left of the split, the $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{C=O}$ fragment comes from a 3-carbon carboxylic acid.
Look closely at the carbon joined to the O on the right, it is joined to three $\text{CH}_3$ groups, so work out which branched butanol that must come from.
walkthrough:
**Split the ester to find its parents**

Remember an ester is made by carboxylic acid + alcohol with water lost. To reverse it, break the single bond between the $\text{C=O}$ carbon and the $\text{O}$.

$$\text{R-C(=O)-O-R'} \rightarrow \text{R-C(=O)-OH} + \text{R'-OH}$$

**Identify the acid fragment on the left**

The left side is $\text{H}_3\text{C-CH}_2\text{-C(=O)-}$. Add back $\text{-OH}$ and you get $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{COOH}$. That is propanoic acid, a straight 3-carbon acid.

**Identify the alcohol fragment on the right**

The right side is $\text{-O-C(CH}_3\text{)}_3$. Add back $\text{H}$ to the O and you get $\text{(CH}_3\text{)}_3\text{COH}$. The OH is on a carbon attached to three other carbons, so this is the tertiary alcohol 2-methylpropan-2-ol.

So the pair is 2-methylpropan-2-ol and propanoic acid.

options.A: Incorrect. Propanoic acid is right for the acid side, but 2-methylpropan-1-ol is $\text{(CH}_3\text{)}_2\text{CHCH}_2\text{OH}$, a primary alcohol. The structure shows the O joined to a carbon with three methyl groups, not a $\text{CH}_2$ group.
options.B: Correct. The $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{C(=O)O-}$ part comes from propanoic acid, and the $\text{-C(CH}_3\text{)}_3$ part comes from 2-methylpropan-2-ol, $\text{(CH}_3\text{)}_3\text{COH}$, where the O is attached to a tertiary carbon.
options.C: Incorrect. This swaps the branching to the wrong side. The branched $\text{C(CH}_3\text{)}_3$ group is on the alcohol (O) side, not on the acid (C=O) side, and the left side is straight, not branched.
options.D: Incorrect. The alcohol 2-methylpropan-2-ol is right, but ethanoic acid is $\text{CH}_3\text{COOH}$ with only 2 carbons. The acid side here clearly has $\text{CH}_3\text{-CH}_2\text{-C=O}$, which is 3 carbons long.
